editorial:
Imagine finding an old, broken video camera that shows you things you aren't supposed to see. That is exactly what happens to Tyler, a star football player, and his little sister Lucy. While Tyler discovers his teammates are being mean to a new kid named Cory, Lucy finds strange clues about Cory's hidden past. It is a real nail-biter because Tyler has to decide if winning a big championship is more important than being a good person. You will feel the tension as he struggles to do the right thing while his friends put pressure on him to stay quiet.

The acting is solid, and having Faith Ford in the mix adds a great touch of warmth to the family scenes. While the plot moves a bit slowly at times, the mystery of the camera keeps you interested. It is a great pick for a family movie night because it teaches a strong lesson without feeling like a lecture. You should definitely try to find this to stream in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video if you can, or just grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to get the best picture quality possible.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when Tyler finally stands up for Cory and exposes the bullies, choosing kindness over the football trophy. Meanwhile, Lucy helps Cory discover the truth about his family through the camera's footage. The mystery wraps up with Cory finding a sense of belonging and peace. The movie ends on a happy note, showing that honesty and bravery lead to better rewards than any sports trophy ever could.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family dramas with a supernatural twist.
